Katie — thanks for the clear checklist. See answers inline and attached prototype manifest.

- Bundle contents: bundle-manifest-v1.3.json (attached), sealed image tar (signed-image.tar, not attached here), and a detached PGP signature (signed-image-sig.asc). The manifest contains image SHA256, model version, quantization profile, and target device artifact IDs.

- Chain-of-custody: we will provide chain-of-custody-form.pdf signed by SecureTransit courier upon pickup; an electronic copy will be uploaded to the shared drive (link below) after the handoff and again when received by the depot.

- ETA: SecureTransit is scheduled for pickup 2026-09-04 18:00 PDT. Transit to ACME-SEA-1 estimated 2026-09-06 by 16:00 local.

Offline verification steps for your operators (summary):
1) Verify manifest SHA against signed-image.tar (sha256).
2) Verify detached signature: gpg --verify signed-image-sig.asc signed-image.tar
3) Check model metadata in manifest (model id/version/quant profile) matches expected.
4) Run staged activation in validation namespace (container runtime) using our provided operator runbook.

I've attached the manifest and included the Drive folder link where we will stage the scanned chain-of-custody PDF after pickup. Marissa — can you confirm operator-runbook version and whether we need additional test vectors in the bundle?

Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/ACME-closed-network

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Request: closed-network bundle handoff for upcoming validation — operator acceptance checklist

Fwd (internal checklist) — Vanessa, Katie: copying the on-policy acceptance steps we ask site operators to perform when they receive sealed bundles. Please confirm if ACME wants any extra logs captured during initial activation.

Operator acceptance checklist (short):
- Unseal courier bag and confirm courier signature on chain-of-custody-form.pdf
- Compute SHA256 of signed-image.tar and compare with manifest entry (bundle-manifest-v1.3.json)
- gpg --keyring /opt/redwood/keys/acme.gpg --verify signed-image-sig.asc signed-image.tar
- Run signature validation script: /opt/redwood/bin/verify_bundle.sh --manifest bundle-manifest-v1.3.json
- Boot into validation namespace and run smoke-test set: smoke/v1/basic-latency, smoke/v1/quant-check (these are included in the bundle as tarred test vectors)
- Capture operator acceptance log: /var/log/redwood/acceptance-<site>-<date>.log and upload to the secure drive (instructions in runbook)

Attachments to include in physical handoff:
- signed-image.tar (large binary - not sent over email)
- signed-image-sig.asc (detached signature)
- bundle-manifest-v1.3.json (attached earlier)
- chain-of-custody-form.pdf (to be signed at pickup by courier)

If SecureTransit can produce a scanned copy at pickup and again on delivery that would save the site operator time. Ops — confirm scanned PDF will be uploaded to the Drive link.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, On-Prem Deployments | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
